summary_paragraph: A woman with type I diabetes was admitted for diabetic ketoacidosis due to severe hyperglycemia with a blood glucose of 706 and an elevated anion gap. She reported a brief episode of chest tightness, which was evaluated and determined to be non-cardiac, likely related to anxiety or metabolic stress. She was treated with IV fluids and an insulin drip, which was transitioned to subcutaneous Lantus and Novolog. Her renal function, initially impaired due to dehydration, improved with hydration. Her chronic back pain was managed with IV then oral pain medication, but no additional narcotics were provided at discharge. She was discharged home in stable condition with updated insulin dosing and instructions to follow up with her diabetes and primary care providers.
